scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported 1492 to 1500 interval is map coverage, not the lifetime of the Ais. No invented founding or extinction date is supplied.
Herman’s Bay is regional archaeological context. Its project report does not make an Ais ethnic attribution.
Field Manor’s proposed Savochequeya identification is retained as tentative. Its duplicated bottom-of-midden wording makes the reported radiocarbon range ambiguous, so that range is omitted.

Dickinson’s 1700 edition describes events in 1696. Printed pages 43, 44 and 48 were checked against page images. His hostile colonial descriptions and cannibalism allegations are not adopted as facts.
Observations at Jece are separated from the earlier episodes at Jobe among the Jaega. No Jaega practice is silently reassigned to the Ais.
The author-posted dissertation abstract was read; the full inaccessible dissertation is not represented as inspected.
Worth’s 1711 population figure concerns a mixed refugee town. His 1760 Keys evacuation and 1763 mission migration do not independently identify the destination of every Ais family.

EBSCO and Field Manor offer simplified or conflicting endings. The card instead uses the specific Ais refugee evidence in Worth and openly limits its conclusion. Independent historical and geographical review remains pending.
